subject: Real-time inference SLA & burst capacity qualification
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Chen <emma@nimbly.ai>, Rajesh Patel <rajesh@nimbly.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 25 Jun 2026 15:05:00 -0700
Subject: Real-time inference SLA & burst capacity qualification

Hi Emma / Rajesh —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we’re aligned. I captured the items we agreed on and a lightweight pilot approach below.

Call summary (high level):
- Primary pain: inconsistent streaming latency under load causing poor live UX (chat and live transcription).
- Current stack: client app -> Node.js API layer -> Redis prefix-cache -> OpenAI hosted endpoints for generation.
- Observed metrics they shared: p95 end-to-end streaming response currently ~400–500ms, occasional spikes >1s under burst.
- Target: p95 <= 200ms for token streaming start and sustained per-token latency such that the UI shows progressive tokens with minimal stutter.
- Concurrency: steady-state 2k concurrent streaming sessions, peak bursts up to ~5k sessions (short duration, 1–3min).
- Cost sensitivity: want predictable unit economics — simple model to compare Redwood Dedicated vs. current hosted spend for 1M tokens/day.

Success criteria (from Emma):
- p95 time-to-first-token for streaming <= 200ms across the steady-state load.
- Under burst (5k sessions) no more than 2x degradation and no errors/timeouts.
- Clear tracing showing which part of the stack contributes to latency (network vs. serving vs. tokenization).

Proposed pilot (what Redwood can do):
1) 2-week dedicated trial: provision a small Dedicated pool with streaming-optimized model variant.
2) Preload KV/prefix cache with top 50 prompts (we’ll provide prompt set).
3) Run synthetic load tests that mirror your session size and token lengths (Aditya will own test harness).
4) Instrumentation: we’ll push per-request traces and token-timing breakdowns; you get a short dashboard and raw traces.
5) Outcome: measurement report, recommended configuration (batching + KV settings + quantization tradeoffs), and a cost projection for 1M/5M tokens/month.

Immediate asks from us (items you agreed to):
- Share the sanitized prompt set and 1-minute sample traces (attached: prompts-sample.txt).
- Fill the tiny SLA worksheet I attached (nimbly-sla-requirements.xlsx) with your absolute must-haves and preferred windows for a 2-week pilot.
- Confirm a pilot start date window (we suggested as early as 2026-07-06).

Next steps / owners:
- Emma/Rajesh: send the prompt set and SLA workbook (you mentioned procurement may need a PO; that’s fine for pilot).
- Aditya (redwood): build the load harness and initial config.
- Monica (redwood): draft the pilot MOU and telemetry access (DocuSign link if needed).
- Ben: coordinate kickoff and measurement criteria.

Attachments: nimbly-sla-requirements.xlsx (SLA workbook), prompts-sample.txt (sample prompts), call-recording-0625.mp3 (internal stub).

Thanks — will follow up with a calendar invite for an internal kickoff once we have the prompts.

Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

From: Emma Chen <emma@nimbly.ai>

Subject: Re: Real-time inference SLA & burst capacity qualification

Thanks Ben — helpful recap. A few clarifications and additional numbers from our side: 

- Current p95 measured at the client (post-network) is ~420ms; server-side logs (we pulled) show ~260ms in the model call for initial tokens; network and client-side processing account for the rest.
- Typical response size: 20–60 tokens for short answers, 150–400 tokens for summary/transcript generation. Average tokens per session ~120.
- Concurrency profile: 2k steady, bursts to 5k for live events (bursts last ~2–5 minutes).
- Error budget: we can tolerate <0.5% 5xx during steady-state; <2% during short bursts.

We uploaded the prompt set and a sanitized trace bundle to the Drive link you provided (same as your related_links). I attached the SLA workbook filled with our initial requirements — mostly must-haves around p95 target and traceability. Procurement is looped in (Rajesh) — they’ll check pricing model options (trial PO may be needed).

Two questions for Redwood: 
1) For streaming UX, can you provide token-level latency histograms out-of-the-box or will that require extra instrumentation on our side?
2) If we run the pilot on Dedicated, what is the expected cold-start behavior for model shards when we hit the 5k burst? Do you have an estimate for warm-up time / memory preloading?

Appreciate the clear plan — we’re keen to see the token-timing breakdown.

—Emma

Ben / Aditya —

Nice summary. Quick internal alignment and a suggested pilot checklist before we kick off: 

Pilot checklist (internal):
- Test harness: Aditya to create two scenarios (steady 2k sessions; burst to 5k for 5 minutes). Include token distribution matching Emma’s samples.
- Observability: enable per-token timing and per-request trace. If Nimbly can’t surface client timings, we’ll add a lightweight JS SDK instrument to capture TTF-token at the client.
- Cache strategy: pre-warm top 50 prompts; configure prefix caching + KV TTLs.
- Fallbacks: configure automatic fallback to lower-capacity shard pool + circuit-breaker thresholds to avoid cascading errors in app.
- Reporting: measurement deck at end of pilot with p50/p95/p99 token timings, error rates, and recommendations.

Permissions/Access: Ben — please confirm we have access to the Drive link and the filled SLA workbook (Emma uploaded). Rajesh — if procurement needs a pilot PO or MSA, let us know constraints.

Proposed timeline: 
- 2026-07-06: pilot provisioning and internal validation (warm-up).
- 2026-07-07 to 2026-07-20: two-week trial with scheduled load windows.
- 2026-07-23: delivery of measurement report and next steps.

I’ll draft a short MOU and share via DocuSign once the SLA workbook is final. Aditya, I’ll hand the harness details to you after Ben confirms the prompt set directory.

Monica Patel
Director, Solutions & Customer Reliability | Redwood Inference
